name: Jira
description: Wakes an agent when something happens on a Jira Cloud issue — a status change, a new issue, a comment or another field change — and lets it read what happened, comment, rewrite the description and move the ticket on. A Team Admin binds their team's Jira site and a service-account API token (used for automated runs and watching projects only — in a chat turn every member's own Jira token is used) and configures which projects to watch, which kinds of event each forwards and which status transitions matter (e.g. "In Progress → Ready for Dev"); the broker sidecar holds that credential and polls Jira server-side, so the token never reaches your browser or an agent container. On a matching event the broker wakes the granted agents and queues the event; the agent drains the queue with the `aee-jira inbox` command-line tool and acts with `aee-jira comment` / `update` / `transition`. This replaces the reverted built-in Jira integration (PR #1539) with an installable, uninstallable plugin — removing it leaves the platform byte-identical. Jira Server / Data Center is not supported; there is no two-way sync.

credentials.label: Jira site
credentials.description: Required for all Jira use (chat and automated). Your Jira Cloud site — a bare subdomain ("acme") or a full origin ("https://acme.atlassian.net")

credentials.label: Service-account e-mail
credentials.description: Only for automated runs and watching projects — the service account's Atlassian e-mail (Basic-Auth username for its API token). Chat turns never use it: each member adds their own under Connections → Plugin Tokens

credentials.label: Service-account API token
credentials.description: Only for automated runs and watching projects — the service account's Jira API token, held only by the broker sidecar, never returned after it is set

credentials.label: Readable custom fields
credentials.description: Optional: comma-separated custom field names agents may read (e.g. "Team, Sprint"), surfaced by default on show/search/list; leave blank to require an explicit --fields per read

credentials.label: Writable custom fields
credentials.description: Optional: comma-separated custom field names agents may SET via `aee-jira set-field` (e.g. "Team"); leave blank to allow writing any custom field. A non-empty list restricts writes to only the named fields

personalCredentials.label: Your Atlassian e-mail
personalCredentials.description: Your Atlassian account e-mail — the Basic-Auth username for your API token

personalCredentials.label: Your API token
personalCredentials.description: Your personal Jira API token (id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens). Used only for Jira calls an agent makes in a chat turn you started; nobody else can read it, admins included

events.name: status_changed
events.description: A watched issue moved to another status

payload.description: the status the issue moved into

events.name: issue_created
events.description: A new issue was created in a watched project

payload.description: human, or agent when an agent created it with aee-jira create-epic, add-stories or create-issue — filter origin = human so an agent does not wake on its own tickets
the status it was created in

events.name: field_changed
events.description: Another field of a watched issue changed (assignee, sprint, …)

payload.description: the field's name as Jira reports it
the field's stable id — use it for custom fields, whose names vary per site
the new value (display text; empty when cleared)
the previous value (display text; empty when it was unset)
human, or agent when an agent set it (aee-jira set-field / attachment add) — filter origin = human so an agent does not wake on its own edits

events.name: comment_added
events.description: Someone commented on a watched issue

payload.description: human, or agent for a comment an agent posted with aee-jira comment — filter origin = human, or an agent wakes on its own comments

promptLine: When something happens on a watched Jira issue you are woken — the wake payload's `event` says what: `status_changed`, `issue_created`, `comment_added` (the comment text is in `body`; `bodyTruncated` means read it in full with `aee-jira show <issueKey> --comment <commentId>`) or `field_changed` (`field`, `from`, `to`); `origin: agent` marks an event your team's own `aee-jira` write caused. Read `event` before acting, then work it with `aee-jira`: `aee-jira inbox` (peek the team's queued events) / `aee-jira inbox --consume <id>…` (drain exactly the ids from your own wake payload: `id`, or `events[].id` in a digest — never a bare `--consume`), `aee-jira list --project KAN [--status "Ready for Dev"]`, `aee-jira search --jql "<JQL>" [--fields …] [--limit N]` (run any JQL, scoped to your team's bound site & projects — for queries `list` can't express, e.g. a `created` date range, an empty custom field, or a summary match; a `--fields` name that isn't a standard column is read as a custom field and rides alongside the row), `aee-jira show KAN-6 [--fields "Team"]` (also lists attachments, the `parent`/epic key — `show` that key to walk Story→Epic — and `availableTransitions`, the moves reachable from the issue's current status so you can pick a `transition --to` without guessing; `--fields` additionally reads custom fields by their Jira name, e.g. `Team` — an empty field comes back as `null`, so you can tell unset from set), `aee-jira link KAN-1 blocks KAN-2` (link two existing issues — read it as a sentence: the first key is the subject of the phrase, so `aee-jira link KAN-2 is blocked by KAN-1` records the same link; a type name such as `Blocks` means its outward phrase; `aee-jira link-types` lists the site's types; an existing identical link is reported, not duplicated; `show` returns each issue's `links` with an `id` and a `statement`), `aee-jira unlink <linkId>` or `aee-jira unlink KAN-1 blocks KAN-2` (remove a link), `aee-jira statuses --project KAN` (every workflow status the project supports, grouped by issue type — the full set, independent of any one issue's current state), `aee-jira attachment get KAN-6 <id>` (fetch one attachment's content — text inline, binary saved to a file), `aee-jira attachment add KAN-6 <path> [<path>…]` (upload one or more local files as new attachments — the created id + filename come back per file), `aee-jira comment KAN-6 --body "…"`, `aee-jira transition KAN-6 --to "In Progress"`, `aee-jira update KAN-6 --description "…"` (replaces the whole description — keep what the human wrote and add your section; the previous text stays in Jira's history), `aee-jira set-field KAN-6 --field "Team" --value "<id>"` (set a custom field by its Jira name — any custom field is writable by default; if a Team Admin set a non-empty writable-custom-fields list, only those are writable and any other is refused; for an id-bearing field like Team pass the id you read with `show --fields "Team"`; use `--value-json '<json>'` for an exotic field shape; a no-op re-set reports `changed:false`), `aee-jira create-epic --project KAN --file plan.json` (turn one ask into its breakdown: create a single Epic and N child Stories underneath it in one call — payload is JSON from --file or stdin: `{"epic":{"summary":…},"stories":[{"summary":…,"assignee":"<accountId>","status":"In Progress","fields":{"Team":"<id>","Story point estimate":5}}]}`. Only summary is required per issue; `status` is applied as a follow-up transition; custom fields in `fields` are writable by default, same as set-field — a non-empty writable-custom-fields list restricts them. The result reports the Epic key + each Story's key, or a per-Story error — the Epic and other Stories still go through), `aee-jira add-stories --epic KAN-12 --file stories.json` (add new Stories to an Epic that ALREADY exists — never creates an Epic, so use it instead of create-epic when the Epic is there: payload `{"stories":[…]}` with the same per-Story fields as create-epic; the Stories land in the Epic's project; refused before anything is created if the key is missing, outside your team's scope or not an Epic; one call per Epic; `--type Bug` or a per-issue `"type"` creates Bugs, Tasks or any standard type of the project under the Epic instead — an unknown, Epic or sub-task type or a missing required field fails only that issue), `aee-jira set-epic KAN-30 KAN-31 --epic KAN-12` (put issues that ALREADY exist under an Epic, or move them there from another Epic; `aee-jira set-epic KAN-30 --none` takes an issue out of its Epic — refused before anything changes if the target is missing, outside your team's scope or not an Epic; each issue gets its own outcome: added, moved, removed, already under the Epic (a success) or failed with the reason — Epics and sub-tasks are never moved; `show` then reports the new `parent`), `aee-jira edit KAN-10 [--summary "…"] [--assignee <accountId> | --unassign] [--priority High] [--add-label L]… [--remove-label L]… [--set-labels L…] [--add-component C]… [--remove-component C]… [--set-components C…] [--add-fix-version V]… [--remove-fix-version V]… [--set-fix-versions V…] [--due 2026-10-31 | --clear-due]` (change the standard fields of one existing issue, several in one call — applied together in one Jira edit or not at all; --add-/--remove- leave the issue's other values alone, --set- replaces the whole list; labels are single words; priority, components and fix versions go by name — an unknown name is refused with the list of what exists, nothing is created; the result gives each field's old and new value, `unchanged` when it already had that value; a field not on the issue's edit screen is named in the refusal; description and custom fields stay with `update` / `set-field`), `aee-jira create-issue --project KAN --type Bug --summary "…" [--description "…"] [--assignee <accountId>] [--priority High] [--label web]… [--field "Team=42"]… [--status "In Progress"]` (create ONE standalone issue without an Epic — a bug report, a task, a single Story: `--type` is the project's own type name, case-insensitive; returns the new key + URL; refused before anything is created if the project is outside your team's scope, the type is unknown (the error lists the project's types), an Epic (use create-epic) or a sub-task, or a required field is missing (the error names it); if the `--status` move fails the issue still exists and `statusError` says why), `aee-jira sprint list --board "<board name>"` (list a Scrum board's sprints — id, name, state, start/end — resolved by the board's human name), `aee-jira sprint create --board "<board name>" --name "<name>" --start 2026-10-26 --end 2026-11-01 [--goal "…"]` (create one future sprint), `aee-jira sprint bulk-create --board "<board name>" --name-template "Acc2.0 {MMM}_{weekOfMonth}" --until 2026-12-31 [--cadence-days 7] [--start 2026-10-26] [--goal "…"]` (pre-create a whole run of future weekly sprints up to a target date in one call, continuing by default from the board's latest existing sprint — supply `--start` when the board has none yet; the name template computes each name from the sprint's Monday: `{MMM}`/`{MMMM}` month, `{MM}`/`{M}`, `{YYYY}`/`{YY}`, `{DD}`/`{D}`, `{weekOfMonth}` the Nth-weekday-of-month, `{n}` the batch index — the month comes from the sprint's Monday even when the week crosses into the next month), `aee-jira sprint close --board "<board name>" [--sprint-id <id>]` (complete the board's active sprint — defaults to whichever sprint is active; reports the count of issues left incomplete, which stay on the closed sprint), `aee-jira sprint start --board "<board name>" [--sprint-id <id>]` (activate the board's next future sprint — defaults to the earliest-starting one; refused if the board already has an active sprint or the sprint has no dates), `aee-jira sprint advance --board "<board name>" [--close-id <id>] [--start-id <id>]` (the weekly roll-over in one call: close the active sprint then start the next future one; each half is reported separately, so a partial result — e.g. closed but no future sprint to start — is visible rather than fatal). A transition you make is itself a status change and wakes whichever teammate's trigger names that target status. All Jira access is server-side in the broker; you never see a Jira token. Whose Jira account a call uses is decided by the platform, not by you: in a chat turn it is the person who wrote the message (their own token — reads show what they can see, writes are authored by them); in an automated run (schedule, event, loop, hand-off) it is the team's service account. If a call is refused for a setup reason (the person has no personal Jira token yet, the team's Jira site is not set, or a token was rejected), relay the refusal message verbatim and in full — it already lists EVERY outstanding item and who fixes each (you add your own token under Agent Studio → Connections → Plugin Tokens; a Team Admin sets the team site under Agent Chat → Settings → Plugins). Do not summarise it down to one item, do not add your own diagnosis about team membership, and never retry some other way.
